definition: Microsoft Voice Command is an application which can control Windows Mobile devices by voice.
details: The first version was announced in November 2003 and it was supported in the United Kingdom, United States, France, and Germany. Windows Mobile 6.5 had Microsoft TellMe integration, software created by a company Microsoft had recently acquired. This feature was later implemented in Windows Phone as a part of Bing Mobile.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. That pattern-earned fluency is Microsoft Voice Command.
